skill.name: aws-cost-cleanup

security_audit.summary: Static command detections are mostly Markdown examples, not executable skill code, and the hardcoded links point to AWS resources. The content still includes destructive AWS cleanup workflows, including a Lambda that deletes EBS volumes, so users need approval and validation controls before use.

remediation.issue: Automated deletion examples can remove AWS resources without approval.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit confirmation steps, scoped allowlists, tag requirements, and default dry-run behavior before any delete or release action.

remediation.issue: The front matter labels the skill risk as safe while it includes destructive AWS operations.
remediation.suggestion: Change the declared risk metadata to reflect destructive cloud actions and require manual review before execution.

remediation.issue: Example scripts use placeholder buckets, profiles, and broad account loops.
remediation.suggestion: Require users to set account, region, profile, and resource tag filters before running commands in any environment.

content.value_statement: AWS accounts often accumulate unused resources that increase monthly costs. This skill helps teams find waste, estimate savings, and plan safer cleanup workflows.
actual_capabilities: Lists common AWS cleanup targets, including EBS volumes, snapshots, Elastic IPs, load balancers, NAT gateways, and ENIs.
Provides dry-run style Bash examples for finding unused EBS volumes, old snapshots, and unused Elastic IPs.
Shows an S3 lifecycle policy for storage transitions, old versions, and incomplete multipart uploads.
Includes a Python cost calculator for unattached EBS volumes and unused Elastic IPs.
Outlines a cleanup workflow with discovery, validation, execution, and verification phases.
Provides examples for AWS Organizations cleanup checks and CloudWatch billing alerts.
limitations: The examples require AWS credentials, permissions, account context, and local validation before use.
The skill cannot prove a resource is unused without environment-specific ownership and dependency checks.
Some examples are destructive if changed from dry-run guidance to active deletion.
Cost estimates use simplified pricing assumptions and may not match every AWS region or account.

use_cases.title: Review Monthly Cloud Waste
use_cases.description: Create an inventory of likely unused AWS resources and estimate potential monthly savings before cleanup.

use_cases.title: Prepare Safe Cleanup Scripts
use_cases.description: Adapt dry-run scripts for tagged resources, approved accounts, and controlled maintenance windows.

use_cases.title: Design Cleanup Governance
use_cases.description: Build a review workflow with owner notification, backup checks, approvals, and post-cleanup verification.

prompt_templates.title: Find Cleanup Candidates
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to list likely unused AWS resources. Focus on read-only discovery and explain what each result means.

prompt_templates.title: Estimate Savings
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to estimate monthly and annual savings from unattached EBS volumes and unused Elastic IPs. Include assumptions and review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Controlled Cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a cleanup plan for one AWS account. Include dry-run commands, approval gates, backups, and rollback checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design Cross-Account Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a cross-account cleanup workflow. Require account allowlists, tag filters, owner notification, logging, and manual approval.

output_examples.input: Find all unused resources and calculate potential savings.
output_examples.output: A prioritized cleanup report with EBS, snapshot, Elastic IP, and networking candidates, estimated savings, and review notes.

output_examples.input: Create a safe cleanup process for old snapshots.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step plan with discovery, owner review, retention checks, backup confirmation, approval, deletion timing, and verification.

output_examples.input: Set up monitoring for AWS cost anomalies.
output_examples.output: A monitoring checklist covering billing alerts, thresholds, notification targets, review cadence, and escalation ownership.

best_practices: Start with read-only discovery and dry-run output before any cleanup action.
Use tags, account allowlists, and owner approval to confirm each resource is safe to remove.
Keep backups, audit logs, and verification steps for every cleanup run.
anti_patterns: Do not run deletion commands across production accounts without scoped filters and approvals.
Do not assume an unattached or old resource is unused without checking owners and dependencies.
Do not rely on simplified savings estimates for billing commitments or regional pricing decisions.

faq.question: Does this skill delete AWS resources automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides examples and workflows. Users must decide whether to run or adapt any cleanup command.

faq.question: What AWS services does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers EBS volumes, EBS snapshots, S3 lifecycle cleanup, Elastic IPs, load balancers, NAT gateways, ENIs, and billing alerts.

faq.question: Can it prove a resource is safe to delete?
faq.answer: No. It helps identify candidates, but teams must verify ownership, dependencies, backups, and compliance requirements.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production accounts?
faq.answer: Use it only with strict controls, dry-run review, tagged resources, approvals, and tested rollback procedures.

faq.question: Does it support cross-account AWS cleanup?
faq.answer: It includes an AWS Organizations example, but users must add account allowlists, profile controls, and audit logging.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.
